_about: Diamond electronics milestones and device records. Numbers are as reported by the cited source; research results are not products.

milestones.event: Hydrogen-terminated CVD diamond found to conduct at the surface
milestones.detail: Landstrass & Ravi observe surface conductivity that vanishes after oxidation.
Kawarada et al. build enhancement-mode MESFETs on homoepitaxial diamond using the surface channel.
Koizumi et al. grow P-doped {111} homoepitaxial films: the first reproducible n-type diamond (donor ~0.57 eV deep).
Maier et al. show adsorbed water/air layers accept electrons from H-terminated diamond, leaving holes behind.
Isberg et al. measure 4,500 cm²/V·s electrons and 3,800 cm²/V·s holes in single-crystal CVD diamond.
Strobel et al. show fullerene acceptors on the surface dope diamond; later oxides (MoO₃, V₂O₅) and NO₂ do the same more stably.
Felbinger et al. compare GaN-on-diamond with GaN-on-SiC; diamond lowers channel temperature at the same power.
Matsumoto et al. report a normally-off inversion-mode p-channel MOSFET on n-type diamond.
Schreck et al. explain buried lateral growth on iridium, the mechanism behind wafer-scale single-crystal diamond.

milestones.event: Stable 2DHG with Al₂O₃ for complementary power inverters
milestones.detail: Kawarada et al. use ALD Al₂O₃ to make the hole gas durable.
Diamond Foundry announces a 100 mm heteroepitaxial single-crystal diamond wafer.
Oi et al. (Waseda): 0.7 A from one vertical 2DHG device, −1.5 A from two in parallel; 225 V breakdown on a narrow device.
Power Diamond Systems (Waseda spin-out, founded 2022) demonstrates packaged devices at SEMICON Japan 2025 and partners with JAXA for space testing; commercialization targeted in the 2030s.

dopants_note: Ionization energies used in sim/transistor_sim/dopants.py: boron 0.37 eV (acceptor), phosphorus 0.57 eV (donor), substitutional nitrogen 1.7 eV (donor). Compare boron and phosphorus in silicon at ~0.045 eV.
